title: When the Summer Sings
premise: Juniper Delacroix, a former corporate lawyer turned single father and owner of Salt Hollow's only bookshop, has spent ten years exchanging anonymous letters with a stranger who once talked him off a ledge — letters signed only 'S.' When Sam Aldana, a burned-out investigative journalist, rents the cottage next door to expose the development company poisoning the town's harbor, Juniper discovers his correspondent has been beside him all along. As Sam's investigation threatens the Calder family, whose money quietly funds the town — and whose eldest son, Marcus, is Juniper's old firm's most important client — Juniper must decide whether to hand over the legal evidence he buried years ago to protect his daughter's future. At the last ferry of the season, Juniper chooses truth over safety, testifying to what he knows, and he and Sam finally stop writing and start living.
about_author: Jonah Reyes is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent seven years covering coastal zoning boards before turning to fiction. They live on a ferry-served island where they still write letters by hand.

chapters.title: The Ledge Year
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A quiet autumn morning in the bookshop; he rereads the oldest of the anonymous letters that pulled him through his wife's death and his disbarment-adjacent disgrace. His daughter Wren, eight, arranges a window display. Emotional beat: tenderness armored over with routine; establish the letters as his secret lifeline.

chapters.title: A Moving Truck in October
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Someone rents the long-empty Hollis cottage next door. Juniper meets Sam Aldana — guarded, sunburned, carrying boxes of files instead of furniture. Sparks of irritation and curiosity. Beat: first disruption of Juniper's carefully contained life.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Keeps
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Sam surveys Salt Hollow under cover of 'researching a travel piece,' photographing the shuttered cannery and sick coves. Flashback to the story that ended his career at a major paper. Beat: his hunger for redemption mirrors Juniper's need for safety.

chapters.title: Wren's Library Card
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Wren befriends Sam when he wanders into the shop seeking shelter from rain. Juniper watches his daughter laugh with the stranger and feels something crack open. Beat: found family begins forming before romance does.

chapters.title: Letters, Unsigned
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Juniper writes his annual letter to 'S.'; Sam, alone at night, writes back to a stranger he's never stopped writing to since the night he talked a suicidal man through a phone line crisis ten years ago. Neither knows the other is next door. Dramatic irony established. Beat: longing across an invisible wall.

chapters.title: The Calder Gala
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The town's benefactors, the Calders, host their charity dinner; Juniper attends out of obligation and runs into Marcus Calder, his old law-school friend and current client of his former firm. Marcus warns him, silkily, about the journalist sniffing around. Beat: power enters the room wearing a smile.

chapters.title: Rain on the Cottage Roof
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. A storm knocks out power; Juniper brings candles and soup. Long conversation on the porch, almost-confessions, charged proximity. Sam nearly mentions the letters, then doesn't. Beat: intimacy without disclosure — the ache of nearness.

chapters.title: Evidence in a Shoebox
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Alone, Juniper retrieves the shoebox of documents from his lawyer days — internal memos proving Calder Development knew the harbor was contaminated a decade ago. He buried them to keep custody of Wren. Beat: the past stops staying past.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Sam learns the ferry line suspends service after November 15 — his deadline, self-imposed, before the town closes like a fist. He publishes nothing yet; sources go silent after a threatening visit from Calder security. Beat: rising stakes, isolation tightening.

chapters.title: Two Handwritings
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Wren finds a discarded draft letter in Sam's recycling while collecting kindling — the handwriting matches 'S.' Juniper confronts the impossible truth and says nothing, terrified of being known that completely. Beat: revelation withheld; fear of exposure.

chapters.title: Marcus Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Marcus offers to buy the bookshop's building at triple value — a gilded bribe to push Juniper out of town before testimony season. Juniper refuses, and understands he's now a target. Beat: corruption shows its face; Juniper's spine stiffens.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Question at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the exposed tidal flats, Sam asks Juniper why he really left the law. Juniper tells the truth about the memos — everything but the letters. Sam realizes Juniper is his source and his neighbor and possibly his letter-writer all at once. Beat: collision of secrets; the midpoint turn toward trust.

chapters.title: What S. Never Said
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Sam confirms via an old postmark that Juniper is 'J.,' the man he saved. He wrestles with whether telling Juniper will feel like a trap or a homecoming. Meanwhile his editor demands the story now. Beat: vulnerability on both sides of the wall.

chapters.title: Confession by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper decides to speak first. In the shop after closing, he lays a decade of letters on the counter. Sam answers by laying his own stack beside them. Ten years collapse into one room. First kiss. Beat: catharsis; the heart's containment fails gloriously.

chapters.title: The Story Breaks Wrong
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Sam's article publishes prematurely — leaked, edited, stripped of the strongest evidence — making Sam look reckless and Juniper look complicit. The town turns cold; the bookshop's windows are chalked with slurs. Beat: false defeat; trust tested by public shame.

chapters.title: Custody Shadows
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Marcus's lawyers file a motion painting Juniper as unstable — citing the letters, his 'obsessive correspondence,' his association with a disgraced reporter. Juniper faces losing Wren for telling the truth. Beat: the cost of justice made personal and brutal.

chapters.title: The Town Decides
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Instead of retreating, neighbors rally: the fisherman whose son got sick, the librarian, Wren's teacher. They bring their own records to the shop, which becomes an unofficial archive. Beat: found family becomes a movement; justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Archive
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Sam and Juniper retrieve the original unredacted lab reports from the county records annex before Calder's people can destroy them — a tense, near-catastrophic break-in. Beat: climax approaches; both men fully committed, no exits left.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Custody hearing and public inquiry collide. Juniper takes the stand, hands over the shoebox, and speaks plainly about what he buried and why. Marcus unravels on cross-examination. Beat: climax — truth spoken at maximum personal cost.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Cleared and vindicated, Sam is offered his old job back in the city. He stands at the dock as the final ferry loads, choosing between the career that saved him and the life next door. He misses the boat on purpose. Beat: romantic resolution; the choice made visible.

chapters.title: Winter Arrives Gently
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. First snow. Sam moves his boxes — real furniture this time — into the cottage for good. Wren claims the reading nook as shared territory. The harbor cleanup begins under court order. Beat: warmth earned; found family settled into daily shape.

chapters.title: When the Summer Sings
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, epilogue. The following June: the bookshop hosts the town's first harbor festival; Sam's follow-up reporting wins an award he keeps in the stockroom. Juniper writes one last letter to 'S.' and delivers it by hand, upstairs, where Sam already knows every word. Beat: full-circle peace; the heart, trainable no longer, simply open.
